Add, index and strip the package's geospatial columns

Source: R/geo-verbs.R
rcs_geo_add.Rd

In-memory verbs that prepare an sf object the way store_write() does, without contacting a store, and take a dataset read from a store back to its raw form. They keep the row order and the column order of x; new columns go immediately before the active geometry column.

Usage

rcs_geo_add(
  x,
  h3_res = 5L,
  bbox = TRUE,
  parents = NULL,
  geocode_engine = c("auto", "s2", "planar"),
  replace = FALSE
)

rcs_geo_index(
  x,
  id,
  h3_res = 5L,
  geocode_engine = c("auto", "s2", "planar"),
  crossing_only = TRUE
)

rcs_geo_strip(x, columns = NULL)

Arguments

x

An sf object with a CRS.

h3_res

H3 resolution of the cells, 0 to 15. For rcs_geo_add(), NULL adds no cell column.

bbox

TRUE adds the column bbox.

parents

Resolutions below h3_res to add as h3_p<r> columns, or NULL.

geocode_engine

How the cells of geometries that cross cell edges are computed: "auto", "s2" or "planar", as in store_write().

replace

A column that is already in x with other values aborts unless replace = TRUE, which recomputes it; one with equal values is kept.

id

Name of the column of x that identifies its rows.

crossing_only

TRUE lists only the rows that touch more than one cell (as a dataset's index table does); FALSE adds one line per other row, with its cell and share = 1.

columns

Names of the columns to drop; NULL drops .rcs_id, h3, h3_main, bbox, every h3_p<r>, and geom unless it is the active geometry column.

Value

rcs_geo_add() and rcs_geo_strip(): x with the columns added or removed. rcs_geo_index(): a tibble with the column id, then h3 (a cell the row touches), h3_main (the row's own cell; both rcs_h3) and share (the fraction of the row's area or length in that cell; 1 / n for points), ordered by row of x, then cell.

Details

  • rcs_geo_add() adds h3 (class rcs_h3: the H3 cell at h3_res holding the largest part of each geometry), one h3_p<r> per resolution r in parents (the parent of h3 at that resolution, for grouping and partitioning) and bbox (a data-frame column with xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax in the CRS of x). The values equal those a write with the same h3_res and geocode_engine computes, so prepared data can be written as they are.

  • rcs_geo_index() gives the cells each geometry touches: one line per row and cell, as the index table of a dataset holds them, keyed by a column of x instead of the package's row identifier.

  • rcs_geo_strip() removes the package's columns, so that a dataset read with collect() goes back to the form it was written from.

Geometries invalid on the sphere are handled as in store_write() (see its argument geocode_engine); one warning names their row numbers.

Prepared writes

store_write() accepts the result of rcs_geo_add(): it drops .rcs_id, computes h3 and bbox itself and compares them with the supplied ones. Equal values are accepted silently, so that raw and prepared writes of the same data give the same version; different values abort (class rcs_error_prepared) naming the first rows and the engine of the write. h3_res is taken from the supplied cells when the write does not give it. The h3_p<r> columns are stored as user columns; with partition = "h3", one equal to the partition column the write chooses serves as it.

Round trip

For store_write(st, rcs_geo_add(raw), dataset, key = k), rcs_geo_strip(collect(store_open(st, dataset))) ordered by k equals raw ordered by k: the same attributes, identical WKB geometries and the same CRS.

See also

store_write(), which accepts prepared data and checks them; vignette("geospatial").

Examples

raw <- rcs_sim_polygons(20, seed = 1)

prepared <- rcs_geo_add(raw, h3_res = 5, parents = 3)
